clue.text: Trip with many stops, taking in different kinds of fare?

definitions.text: Trip with many stops, taking in different kinds of fare?

parts.words: Trip with many stops, taking in different kinds of fare?
parts.note: a bus driver makes many stops and takes fares all day; a holiday spent doing the same sort of thing as your job is named after that worker

explanation.surface: A tour that keeps halting so travellers can sample a variety of local food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' looks like food on a gastronomic tour, but it is the money a bus driver collects at every stop.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a break spent doing much the same work as one's ordinary job, like a bus driver taking a coach trip.

clue.text: Like human or ape build, not universal, unfortunately

indicators.note: something that has gone unfortunately has gone wrong, so the remaining letters are jumbled
not tells us to leave a letter out of the words ape build

parts.note: U is the film-certificate abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: Building something like a human or an ape, minus anything universal, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes U from APEBUILD, leaving APEBILD, which 'unfortunately' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Humans walk upright on two legs, so a two-footed description fits them.

clue.text: Mother's arguing sadly about a daughter's misfortune?

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the next piece
things gone sadly have gone amiss, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A mother quarrelling unhappily over some misfortune that has befallen her daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges MOTHERS ARGUING, and 'about' puts that around A.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding forced on a pregnant young woman by her family is, the question mark admits, a playful view of her bad luck.

clue.text: Athletic's modus operandi, playing at United?

parts.note: A abbreviates Athletic, as in football club names
a modus operandi is a way of doing things

explanation.surface: How a football side called Athletic sets out its tactics when visiting United.
explanation.walkthrough: Many English football clubs are called Athletic (Charlton, Wigan) or United; a match on the other side's ground is an away game.
explanation.definitionFit: A team visiting another club's ground is not at home, so playing at United's stadium is an example.

clue.text: Fail to take in location of bars around centre of Perth

indicators.note: around means the stave goes on either side of the next letter

parts.note: musical bars are written on a stave

indicators.note: centre of picks the middle letter of the word Perth

explanation.surface: Not managing to visit the area of Perth's town centre where the pubs are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bars' look like pubs but are bars of music, set on a stave.
explanation.definitionFit: To go without nourishment is to fail to take in food, so the phrase works as a verb.

clue.text: Newspaper to stop producing fine material

parts.note: an organ is a newspaper or journal speaking for a group
to die is to stop working, as an engine dies

explanation.surface: A paper is going to cease printing.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheer, stiff muslin used for dresses, a delicate fabric.

clue.text: Perk up and ask about river in Indian territory

indicators.note: about means the word for ask goes around what follows

parts.note: to invite someone is to ask them along

indicators.note: in puts the river's letter inside the Indian territory

parts.note: Goa is a state on India's west coast
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Cheer up, and enquire about a river in some part of India.
explanation.definitionFit: To energise or enliven someone, a synonym of the phrasal verb.

clue.text: Senior lawyer swayed by a longer entreaty?

indicators.note: something swayed is moved about, so these letters shift into a new order

explanation.surface: A top barrister persuaded by an especially long plea, which fits a lawyer's world.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief law officer advising the government is the most senior lawyer in the land.

clue.text: Famous person guided round dirt

indicators.note: round means the word for guided goes around the next piece

parts.note: led means guided
gen is slang for information, like dirt on someone

explanation.surface: A celebrity steered around some muck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dirt' looks like mud, but it is inside information, GEN in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrated figure is called this in the sense of someone renowned in their field.

clue.text: Proportionately based voting system? Men answer with cheers

parts.note: PR is proportional representation
OR is other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
ta is British slang for thanks

explanation.surface: A voting system based on proportions, as soldiers reply with a cheer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proportionately based' looks like it describes the voting system, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase describes something divided in proportion, such as pay scaled to hours worked.

clue.text: Offered to host outrageous dance

indicators.note: to host means to hold another piece inside

parts.note: gave means offered
OTT is over the top, outrageous

explanation.surface: Volunteered to put on an over-the-top dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A French dance of the 18th century in moderate duple time.

clue.text: Likes a place to stay

definitions.meaning: slang: to dig something is to enjoy it
lodgings rented for a while, as a student rents a room

explanation.definitionFit: The slang verb for enjoying, and British slang for rented rooms, share one spelling.

clue.text: A very great and creative description of modern art

indicators.note: being creative with letters means making something new from them

explanation.surface: Praise for modern art as truly great and inventive.
explanation.definitionFit: Experimental, innovative work ahead of its time is labelled this way.

clue.text: Support governors adopting lecturer's teaching aid

indicators.note: adopting means taking the lecturer's letter in

parts.note: to back is to support
L is the abbreviation for lecturer
a school's governors make up its board

explanation.surface: School governors backing a lecturer's teaching aid.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark board written on with chalk is a classic classroom tool.

clue.text: Left just holding end of rope, abandoned

indicators.note: holding means the word for just goes around the next letter

parts.note: only means just

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of rope

explanation.surface: Someone left clinging to the end of a rope, deserted.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone forsaken and alone feels isolated and solitary.

clue.text: Confusion with study restricting entry to harbour and end of jetty

parts.note: pie is printers' jargon for jumbled type, a muddle

indicators.note: restricting means the word for study encloses a letter

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it

indicators.note: entry to picks the first letter of harbour

explanation.surface: Muddle as a survey limits access to a harbour and the end of a jetty.
explanation.definitionFit: The seaward tip of a pier, the far end of a landing stage.

clue.text: Ancient city: a bit of history in horse-drawn era?

indicators.note: in means the letter is put inside

parts.note: a cart age, a time when carts were pulled by horses

indicators.note: a bit of picks the first letter of history

explanation.surface: An ancient city as a slice of history from the days of horse carts.
explanation.definitionFit: The Phoenician city in North Africa destroyed by Rome in 146 BC.

clue.text: Fuel, clean, with poisonous gas entirely cut

parts.note: to char is to clean, as a charwoman does
CO is the formula for carbon monoxide

indicators.note: cut means the word for entirely loses its last letter

parts.note: all means entirely

explanation.surface: Fuel that cleans and slashes poison gas completely.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAR, to do cleaning work, is a British usage, from charwoman.
explanation.definitionFit: Charred wood burnt as a smokeless fuel, as on a barbecue.

clue.text: Redesign coins

definitions.meaning: small money in loose metal pieces

explanation.definitionFit: The verb meaning alter and the noun for loose coins share a spelling.

clue.text: Get money from the old woman, expressing new evidence of nastiness?

indicators.note: expressing means squeezing out, so a letter is pressed out

parts.note: to sting someone is to swindle money from them
MA, mother, is one's old woman

explanation.surface: Wringing cash out of Mum would show a nasty streak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expressing' looks like 'saying', but here it means squeezing out N.
explanation.definitionFit: A mark of disgrace left on someone could be read as a sign of wrongdoing, hence the question mark.

clue.text: A historic murderer runs up tree

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means moving the letter higher, towards the start

parts.note: Brutus was one of the assassins of Julius Caesar
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A famous killer sprints up into a tree to escape.
explanation.definitionFit: The strawberry tree, an evergreen shrub with red berries, is the genus here.

clue.text: Approach some good shots, repeating a couple of components

indicators.note: a couple of components means two of the letters are each given twice

parts.note: aces are unreturned serves at tennis

explanation.surface: A tennis player approaches some fine shots, playing a few strokes again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeating a couple of components' doubles the C and the S of ACES.
explanation.definitionFit: A way in, or a means of reaching somewhere, as in access to a building.

clue.text: Actor with basic manoeuvres — nothing like these!

definitions.note: plural noun: gymnastic feats are anything but basic moves

indicators.note: manoeuvres means the letters are moved about

explanation.surface: An actor with simple moves, nothing like a circus performer's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvres' does double duty: it shuffles the letters and begins the definition, which says these feats are nothing like basic.
explanation.definitionFit: Gymnastic feats such as somersaults are far from simple moves.

clue.text: High-minded type rejected gifts heartlessly

indicators.note: rejected means the remaining letters are thrown back
heartlessly means the middle letter is taken out

parts.note: boons are gifts or blessings

explanation.surface: A haughty person who coldly turned down presents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' drops the middle O of BOONS to give BONS, and 'rejected' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: A superior person who looks down on others, holding their nose high.

clue.text: Cliff foot destroyed in panic

indicators.note: in a down clue the foot is the bottom letter, and it is removed

parts.note: a scare is a panic

explanation.surface: Someone at the bottom of a cliff wrecked by panic.
explanation.definitionFit: A steep rocky outcrop on a hillside, a northern English word for crag.

clue.text: Splendid article about a Spanish city

indicators.note: about means the word for splendid goes round the article

parts.note: grand means splendid
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A grand piece of writing about a city in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andalusian city famed for the Alhambra palace.

clue.text: Passage cut right through bar

indicators.note: through means the letter goes right through, inside the word

parts.note: bar means except, as in all bar one

explanation.surface: A corridor sliced through a bar, perhaps in a pub refurbishment.
explanation.definitionFit: An extract is a section taken out of a longer text.

clue.text: Historic documents found in local addresses after mistake

indicators.note: after a mistake the letters are out of place and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Old papers discovered at nearby addresses after an error.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Jewish manuscripts found in caves at Qumran from 1947.
